content:
Jessica Park: Quick Q — we just moved Priya from Platform -> Infra last week and her manager wants to promote her to L4 effective 3/1. Is there a clean way to do a backdated comp change and equity refresh?
Samir Khan: Hi Jess — possible but depends on timing/approval. Two parts: salary increase + any equity refresh. For pay we usually credit back to the effective date if approved before payroll cutoff.
Maria Lopez: @jessica can you confirm if Priya's new manager started the leveling checklist? Need the evidence packet (role doc, 3 examples of qualifying work, manager rec) before comp review.
Jessica Park: Yep — manager attached a short packet in Google Drive and left notes in the leveling doc. They want to fast-track.
Jordan Lee: Fast-track possible for internal transfers but need exemption if it's mid-cycle (outside standard promo window). That's routed to Comp Committee.
People Ops Bot: Reminder — submit the "Comp Exception" form: https://redwooduniverse/internal/forms/comp-exception. Include: employee ID, current comp, requested comp, effective date, manager justification, evidence link.
Samir Khan: Important: payroll deadlines — if effective date is 3/1 and we want backpay in March payroll, approvals must be complete by EOD on the 10th of March. Otherwise backpay goes into next cycle.
Payroll Team: Also note payroll needs the approved comp_change CSV by 11:59pm PT on the 11th for processing. If there's an equity grant tech hold, equity ops needs ~7 business days after approval to generate docs.
Maria Lopez: For the comp packet: put bullets for impact + metrics, list of comparable peers for leveling rationale, and a short upward manager calibration note. Tiny template: 
```
Role & scope: 
Key outcomes (3 bullets): 
Examples of work + dates: 
Peer comps: names & levels: 
Manager rec & suggested comp band: 
```
Jessica Park: Who signs off on the exception? Manager -> L4+ manager (skip?) -> Comp Committee -> People Ops?
Jordan Lee: Flow is manager -> director -> people-ops lead -> comp committee. If it's a lateral transfer + leveling up in same org director signoff is often enough but still logged with comp committee for transparency.
Samir Khan: If you need immediate temp pay adjustment while committee reviews, we can do a "stop-gap" ad-hoc increase (expires after 90 days) but Comp must retroactively approve for permanent change and backpay. Use only for critical retention risk.
Jessica Park: Good to know. Any caps on how far back we can backpay?
Payroll Team: We generally can backpay up to 90 days retroactive. Anything beyond needs finance sign-off and justification.
Maria Lopez: Equity: if manager requests a refresh outside equity cycle, it triggers a separate equity approval flow. That can be slower — set expectations.
Jessica Park: Thanks. I'll submit the comp-exception form now and ping manager to flesh out the packet. One more — do we tell the employee about the pending retroactive comp now or wait until approvals?
Jordan Lee: Best practice: tell them you're submitting and it's pending approvals; avoid promising backpay until signed off. Keeps communications transparent but cautious.
Jessica Park: Awesome — submitting and tagging you all. Will include manager evidence and requested effective date 2026-03-01.
People Ops Bot: Form submitted by Jessica Park (link: https://redwooduniverse/internal/forms/submissions/238912). Notification sent to comp-committee@redwood.com.
Samir Khan: Thanks. Once Comp Committee has a decision I'll route approved change to payroll and equity ops. If anyone needs a template email to the employee, I can drop one in thread. :thumbsup:
Jessica Park: Please do that template, Samir. Appreciate the help! :pray:
